translations.literal: Soon he was made Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made central army commander.

sentences.zh: 及賀若弼進軍鍾山，廣達率眾於白土崗南置陣，與弼旗鼓相對。

translations.literal: When He Ruo Bi advanced on Bell Mountain, Guangda led troops and set his formation south of White Earth Mound, pennants and drums facing Bi's.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruo Bi advanced on Bell Mountain, Guangda led troops and set his formation south of White Earth Mound, pennants and drums facing Bi's.

sentences.zh: 廣達躬擐甲冑，手執桴鼓，率勵敢死，冒刃而前，隋軍退走，廣達逐北至營，殺傷甚眾，如是者數四焉。

translations.literal: Guangda personally donned armor, hand holding the drum mallet, leading and encouraging the daring dead, braving blades and going forward; the Sui army fell back and fled; Guangda pursued north to their camp and killed and wounded very many—thus several times.
translations.idiomatic: Guangda personally donned armor, drum mallet in hand, leading the daring dead forward through the blades. The Sui army fell back; Guangda pursued to their camp and killed and wounded very many—several times over.

sentences.zh: 及弼攻敗諸將，乘勝至宮城，燒北掖門，廣達猶督餘兵，苦戰不息，斬獲數十百人。

translations.literal: When Bi defeated the generals and pressed the victory to the palace city, burning the North Wing Gate, Guangda still directed the remaining troops in bitter fighting without cease, beheading and capturing several tens and hundreds of men.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi defeated the generals and pressed the victory to the palace city, burning the North Wing Gate, Guangda still directed the remaining troops in bitter fighting and beheaded and captured several tens and hundreds.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，乃解甲，面臺再拜慟哭，謂眾曰：「我身不能救國，負罪深矣。

translations.literal: When evening came he then removed his armor, faced the palace and twice bowed, weeping bitterly, and said to the host: "I myself could not save the state—the guilt is deep.
translations.idiomatic: At evening he removed his armor, faced the palace, bowed twice, and wept bitterly, telling the troops, "I could not save the state—the guilt is deep.

sentences.zh: 」士卒皆涕泣歔欷，於是乃就執。

translations.literal: " The soldiers all wept and sobbed; thereupon they submitted to capture.
translations.idiomatic: " The soldiers all wept and sobbed; thereupon they submitted to capture.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，依例入隋。

translations.literal: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 (589) he entered Sui according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 廣達愴本朝淪覆，遘疾不治，尋以憤慨卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: Guangda grieved that his native dynasty had fallen; he met illness and did not recover, and soon died from indignation, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Guangda grieved his dynasty's fall, fell ill and did not recover, and soon died of indignation at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 尚書令江總撫柩慟哭，乃命筆題其棺頭，為詩曰：「黃泉雖抱恨，白日自流名，悲君感義死，不作負恩生。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Jiang Zong stroked the coffin and wept bitterly; he then ordered a brush to inscribe on the coffin head a poem, saying: "Though the yellow springs hold regret, the white day still leaves a name; I grieve that you died for righteousness moved by duty, not that you lived ungrateful to favor.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat director Jiang Zong stroked the coffin and wept bitterly, then had a poem brushed on the coffin head: "Though the yellow springs hold regret, the white day still leaves a name; I grieve that you died for moved righteousness, not that you lived ungrateful to favor.

sentences.zh: 」總又製廣達墓銘，其略曰：「災流淮海，險失金湯，時屯運極，代革天亡。

translations.literal: " Zong also composed Guangda's tomb inscription; its gist said: "Disaster flowed through the Huai and sea; peril lost metal walls and moats; the time was straitened and fortune exhausted; the age changed and Heaven perished.
translations.idiomatic: " Zong also composed Guangda's tomb inscription, which in gist said, "Disaster flowed through Huai and sea; peril lost metal walls; the time was straitened and fortune exhausted; the age changed and Heaven perished.

sentences.zh: 爪牙背義，介冑無良，獨摽忠勇，率禦有方。

translations.literal: Claws and fangs turned from righteousness; armor and helm knew no worth; alone he raised loyal courage and led defense with method.
translations.idiomatic: Claws and fangs turned from righteousness; armor knew no worth; alone he raised loyal courage and led defense with method.

sentences.zh: 誠貫皎日，氣勵嚴霜，懷恩感報，撫事何忘。」

translations.literal: Sincerity pierced the bright sun; spirit roused the hard frost; cherishing favor he repaid gratitude—how could he forget when he stroked the affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity pierced the bright sun; spirit roused hard frost; cherishing favor he repaid grace—how could he forget what he had undertaken?"

sentences.zh: 初，隋將韓擒虎之濟江也，廣達長子世真在新蔡，乃與其弟世雄及所部奔擒虎，〔擒虎〕遣使致書，〔一八〕以招廣達，〔廣達〕時屯兵京師，〔一九〕乃自劾廷尉請罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sui General Han Qinhu crossed the river, Guangda's eldest son Shizhen was at Xincai; he with his younger brother Shixiong and their following went over to Qinhu; [Qinhu] sent a messenger with a letter, Editorial footnote marker 18. to recruit Guangda; [Guangda] was then garrisoning troops at the capital, Editorial footnote marker 19. and himself impeached himself before the Court Tribunal requesting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sui general Han Qinhu crossed the river, Guangda's eldest son Shizhen was at Xincai; he with his brother Shixiong and their following went over to Qinhu. [Qinhu] sent a letter [18] to recruit Guangda; [Guangda] was then garrisoning at the capital [19] and impeached himself before the court tribunal.

sentences.zh: 後主謂之曰：「世真雖異路中大夫，公國之重臣，吾所恃賴，豈得自同嫌疑之間乎？

translations.literal: Houzhu said to him: "Though Shizhen is on a different path as a middle grandee, you are a heavy minister of the state whom I rely on—how could I treat myself the same as among the suspected?"
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu told him, "Though Shizhen has taken another path as a middle grandee, you are a heavy minister of the state whom I rely on—how could I lump you among the suspected?"

sentences.zh: 」加賜黃金，即日還營。

translations.literal: He additionally bestowed gold, and that same day Guangda returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: He additionally bestowed gold, and that same day Guangda returned to camp.

sentences.zh: 廣達有隊主楊孝辯，時從廣達在軍中，力戰陷陣，其子亦隨孝辯，揮刃殺隋兵十餘人，力窮，父子俱死。

translations.literal: Guangda had a squad leader Yang Xiaobian who was then with Guangda in the army, fighting fiercely and breaking formations; his son also followed Xiaobian, wielding a blade and killing more than ten Sui soldiers; when strength was exhausted, father and son both died.
translations.idiomatic: Guangda had a squad leader Yang Xiaobian then with him in the army, fighting fiercely through the formations; his son followed Xiaobian, blade in hand, and killed more than ten Sui soldiers; when strength was spent, father and son both died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：蕭摩訶氣冠三軍，當時良將，雖無智略，亦一代匹夫之勇矣；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xiao Mohe's spirit crowned the three armies; he was a good general of the time; though he had no strategy, he was still the mere-man courage of a generation;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Xiao Mohe's spirit crowned the three armies; he was a good general of his time; though he had no strategy, he was still the raw courage of a generation;

sentences.zh: 然口訥心勁，恂恂李廣之徒歟。

translations.literal: yet his tongue was slow and his heart firm—was he not of the respectful kind like Li Guang?
translations.idiomatic: yet his tongue was slow and his heart firm—was he not of Li Guang's respectful kind?

sentences.zh: 任忠雖勇決彊斷，而心懷反覆，誣紿君上，自躓其惡，鄙矣！

translations.literal: Ren Zhong, though brave, decisive, and strong in cutting through, yet in his heart harbored reversal; he deceived and beguiled his lord above and stumbled into his own evil—despicable!
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhong was brave and decisive, yet his heart harbored reversal; he deceived his lord and stumbled into his own evil—despicable!

sentences.zh: 至於魯廣達全忠守道，殉義忘身，蓋亦陳代之良臣也。

translations.literal: As for Lu Guangda, he wholly kept loyalty and guarded the Way, dying for righteousness and forgetting his person—he was probably also a good minister of the Chen age.
translations.idiomatic: As for Lu Guangda, he wholly kept loyalty and guarded the Way, dying for righteousness and forgetting himself—probably also a good minister of Chen.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 〔一〕 其姑夫蔡路養時在南康 殿本考證云「姑」南史作「姊」。

translations.literal: [1] His uncle by marriage Cai Luyang was then at Nankang—the Hall edition verification says "aunt" in the Southern History reads "elder sister."
translations.idiomatic: On "his uncle by marriage Cai Luyang was then at Nankang": the Hall edition notes that aunt in the Southern History reads elder sister.

sentences.zh: 按元龜八四七亦作「姊」。

translations.literal: According to the Yuan Gui, 847 also reads "elder sister."
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Gui 847 also reads elder sister.

sentences.zh: 〔二〕 車騎大將軍 按後主紀作「車騎將軍」，詳參卷六後主紀校記一。

translations.literal: [2] Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry—according to the Annals of the Later Lord it reads "General of Chariots and Cavalry"; see Collation Note 1 in the Annals of the Later Lord, Volume 6.
translations.idiomatic: On "[2] grand general of chariots and cavalry": the Annals of Houzhu read general of chariots and cavalry; see Collation Note 1 in Volume 6 of Houzhu's annals.

sentences.zh: 〔三〕 封綏

translations.literal: [3] Enfeoffed as Sui
translations.idiomatic: On "[3] enfeoffed as Sui"

translations.literal: (yuan)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (yuan).

sentences.zh: 〔建〕郡公 據南史改。

translations.literal: [jian] Commandery Duke—changed according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: (jian) Commandery Duke—emended per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 按南朝宋置綏建郡，隋志南海郡四會縣下小注云「舊置綏建郡」。

translations.literal: Comment: the Song of the Southern Dynasties established Suijian commandery; the Sui Treatise under Sihui county of Nanhai commandery has a small note, "formerly Suijian commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Song of the Southern Dynasties established Suijian commandery; the Sui Treatise notes under Sihui in Nanhai, "formerly Suijian commandery."

sentences.zh: 〔四〕 驃騎大將軍 按後主紀作「驃騎將軍」。

translations.literal: [4] Grand General of Agile Cavalry—according to the Annals of the Later Lord it reads "General of Agile Cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: On "[4] grand general of agile cavalry": Houzhu's annals read general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 〔五〕 及

translations.literal: [5] When
translations.idiomatic: On "[5] when"

translations.literal: (Ruo)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Ruo).

sentences.zh: 弼進軍鍾山 按賀若復姓，弼姓賀若，此當單舉其名，明衍「若」字，今刪。

translations.literal: Bi advanced on Bell Mountain—He Ruo is a double surname; Bi's surname is He Ruo; here only the personal name should be cited; clearly "Ruo" was interpolated; it is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: On "Bi advanced on Bell Mountain": He Ruo is a compound surname and Bi's surname is He Ruo; only the personal name should stand; Ruo was clearly interpolated and is now deleted.

sentences.zh: 〔六〕 隨晉熙太守梅伯龍討景將王貴顯於壽春 按「王貴顯」梁書侯景傳及通鑑梁武帝太清二年、三年並作「王顯貴」。

translations.literal: [6] Following Jinxi Administrator Mei Bolong in attacking Jing's general Wang Guixian at Shouchun—according to the Biography of Hou Jing in the Book of Liang and the Comprehensive Mirror in the second and third years of Emperor Wu of Liang's Taiqing, all read "Wang Xian Gui."
translations.idiomatic: On "[6] following Jinxi administrator Mei Bolong in attacking Jing's general Wang Guixian at Shouchun": the Biography of Hou Jing in the Book of Liang and the Comprehensive Mirror for Taiqing years 2–3 of Liang Wudi all read Wang Xian Gui.

sentences.zh: 〔七〕 進軍蘄譙 「蘄」原訛「斬」，據北監本、汲本、殿本改正。

translations.literal: [7] Advancing on Qi and Qiao—"Qi" was originally wrong as "Zhan"; corrected according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[7] advancing on Qi and Qiao": Qi was originally wrong as Zhan and is corrected per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 按南監本「蘄」作「舒」，訛。

translations.literal: Comment: the Southern Supervisory edition reads "Qi" as "Shu"—wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Supervisory edition reads Qi as Shu—an error.

sentences.zh: 〔八〕 改封梁信

translations.literal: [8] Re-enfeoffed as Liangxin
translations.idiomatic: On "[8] re-enfeoffed as Liangxin"

translations.literal: (Du)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Du).

sentences.zh: 郡公 據南史刪。

translations.literal: Commandery Duke—deleted according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery Duke—deleted per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 〔九〕 詔以毅為都督北討前軍事 按宣帝紀，毅於是年為督都北討諸軍事，通鑑同，為都督北討前軍事者乃任忠，非樊毅。

translations.literal: [9] An edict made Yi area commander of the northern expedition vanguard military affairs—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Yi in that year was commander of all northern expedition military affairs; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees; the one who was commander of the northern expedition vanguard military affairs was Ren Zhong, not Fan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On "[9] an edict made Yi commander of the northern expedition vanguard military affairs": Emperor Xuan's annals have Yi that year as commander of all northern expedition military affairs; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees; northern expedition vanguard commander was Ren Zhong, not Fan Yi.

sentences.zh: 此「前」字，當作「諸」。

translations.literal: This character "front" should read "all."
translations.idiomatic: Front here should read all.

sentences.zh: 〔一０〕梁

translations.literal: [10] Liang
translations.idiomatic: On "[10] Liang"

translations.literal: (An)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (An).

sentences.zh: 南〔安〕侯蕭方矩為湘州刺史 據南史改。

translations.literal: Southern [An] Marquis Xiao Fangju was made Inspector of Xiangzhou—changed according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: Southern [An] marquis Xiao Fangju was made inspector of Xiangzhou—emended per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 按梁書愍懷太子方矩傳亦作「南安」。

translations.literal: Comment: the Biography of the Lamented Heir Apparent Fangju in the Book of Liang also reads "Nan'an."
translations.idiomatic: The Biography of the Lamented Heir Apparent Fangju in the Book of Liang also reads Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 〔一一〕光

translations.literal: [11] Guang
translations.idiomatic: On "[11] Guang"

translations.literal: (Lu)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Lu).

sentences.zh: 大

translations.literal: Grand
translations.idiomatic: Grand

translations.literal: (Master)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Master).

sentences.zh: 元年 據南史刪。

translations.literal: first year—deleted according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: First year—deleted per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 按元龜三八０作「少帝光大元年」。

translations.literal: Comment: the Yuan Gui, 380 reads "Young Emperor's Guangda first year."
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Gui 380 reads "Young Emperor's Guangda first year."

sentences.zh: 〔一二〕斬其敷城王張元範 按「王」各本及南史並作「主」。

translations.literal: [12] Beheading their Fucheng King Zhang Yuanfan—according to all editions and the Southern History, "king" reads "lord."
translations.idiomatic: On "[12] beheading their Fucheng king Zhang Yuanfan": all editions and the Southern History read lord for king.

sentences.zh: 據魏書地形志，晉州有敷城郡及敷城縣，肆州秀容郡有敷城縣，皆在今山西省境。

translations.literal: According to the Treatise on Geography in the Book of Wei, Jin province had Fucheng commandery and Fucheng county; Xi province's Xiurong commandery had Fucheng county—all in present-day Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Geography in the Book of Wei places Fucheng commandery and county in Jin province and another Fucheng in Xiurong of Xi—all in present Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 大峴在合肥之南，歷陽之北，其地附近郡縣無名敷城者，疑作「王」是。

translations.literal: Great Xian lies south of Hefei and north of Liyang; in the nearby commanderies and counties there is none named Fucheng; it is suspected that "king" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Great Xian lies south of Hefei and north of Liyang; nearby commanderies have no Fucheng; king is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 北齊季世，王封甚濫，張保洛齊世封敷城郡王，時已卒，元範或即保洛子嗣封者。

translations.literal: In the late Northern Qi, kingly enfeoffments were very lavish; Zhang Baoluo in Qi times was enfeoffed as King of Fucheng commandery and had already died; Yuanfan may be a successor son who inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Late Northern Qi enfeoffed kings lavishly; Zhang Baoluo of Qi was enfeoffed king of Fucheng commandery and had died; Yuanfan may be a successor who inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 〔一三〕〔北〕徐州刺史 據南史補。

translations.literal: [13] [North] Inspector of Xuzhou—supplied according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: On "[13] [north] inspector of Xuzhou": supplied per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 〔一四〕南北兗晉等各〔自〕拔 據北監本、汲本、殿本及南史補。

translations.literal: [14] South Yan, North Yan, Jin, and the rest each [withdrew] of themselves—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: On "[14] South Yan, North Yan, Jin, and the rest each withdrew of themselves": supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 〔一五〕十二年與豫州刺史樊毅率眾北討 「豫州」南史作「南豫州」。

translations.literal: [15] In the twelfth year, with Inspector of Yu Fan Yi he led troops on the northern expedition—"Yu" in the Southern History reads "Southern Yu."
translations.idiomatic: On "[15] in year 12 with Yu inspector Fan Yi on the northern expedition": Yu in the Southern History reads Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 按樊毅傳，毅於此時無為豫州或南豫州刺史事。

translations.literal: According to the Biography of Fan Yi, at this time Yi was neither Inspector of Yu nor of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yi's biography shows he was neither Yu nor Southern Yu inspector at this time.

sentences.zh: 張森楷校勘記疑「樊毅」為「樊猛」之訛。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai's collation note suspects "Fan Yi" is an error for "Fan Meng."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai's collation suspects Fan Yi is an error for Fan Meng.

sentences.zh: 然按樊猛傳，猛為南豫州刺史在後主至德四年，與此不合。

translations.literal: Yet according to the Biography of Fan Meng, Meng as Inspector of Southern Yu was in Houzhu's fourth year of Zhide, which does not match this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fan Meng's biography has him as Southern Yu inspector in Houzhu's Zhide year 4, which does not match.

sentences.zh: 或疑「樊毅」為「任忠」之訛，以忠於太建十二年遷南豫州刺史也。

translations.literal: Some suspect "Fan Yi" is an error for "Ren Zhong," since Zhong in the twelfth year of Taijian was moved to Inspector of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Some suspect Fan Yi should be Ren Zhong, made Southern Yu inspector in Taijian year 12.

sentences.zh: 〔一六〕都督郢州以上十州諸軍事 「十州」南史作「七州」。

translations.literal: [16] Area Commander over the military affairs of the ten provinces above Ying—"ten provinces" in the Southern History reads "seven provinces."
translations.idiomatic: On "[16] commander over the military affairs of the ten provinces above Ying": ten provinces in the Southern History reads seven provinces.

sentences.zh: 〔一七〕周安州總管元景將兵寇江外 按元景隋書有傳，作「元景山」。

translations.literal: [17] Zhou's Anzhou Area Commander Yuan Jing led troops to raid the lands outside the river—according to the Biography of Yuan Jing in the Book of Sui, it reads "Yuan Jingshan."
translations.idiomatic: On "[17] Zhou's Anzhou area commander Yuan Jing raided lands outside the river": the Book of Sui biography reads Yuan Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 〔一八〕〔擒虎〕遣使致書 據北監本、汲本、殿本及南史補。

translations.literal: [18] [Qinhu] sent a messenger with a letter—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: On "[18] [Qinhu] sent a messenger with a letter": supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 〔一九〕〔廣達〕時屯兵京師 據北監本、汲本、殿本及南史補。

translations.literal: [19] [Guangda] was then garrisoning troops at the capital—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: On "[19] [Guangda] was then garrisoning at the capital": supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the Southern History.
